Below is an essay you revised once. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 393 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Essay:

Dear Principal,

I am writing about if our school should make every student do community service. I think it should not be a requirement, but the school should really encourage it and make it easy to do.

My friends who volunteer are proud of it. One helps third graders with reading after school, and she says the kids light up when a hard word finally clicks for them. Another one goes to a litter cleanup on weekends at the creek by our neighborhood. They both feel like helping others matters, and I agree. Service teaches you to be responsible and patient and that you are part of something bigger than just yourself.

But a requirement would cause some problems. A lot of students already have really full schedules. Some have part-time jobs to help their families pay bills. Others take care of their little brothers and sisters or play on teams that practice every single day. For these students, a service quota would just be one more thing on time they barely have. My friend works at a grocery store four nights a week. If you tell him to find extra hours for service, it would only stress him out and it might hurt his grades.

Also, there is the problem of why people do it. When something is forced, lots of people just do the bare minimum and watch the clock. A student who has to sign a log sheet might start to hate volunteering instead of liking it. Service that comes from your own choice usually means more, to the student and to the people who get helped.

Instead of a requirement, I think the school should make better chances for students to help. We could have a volunteer fair where local groups like food banks, libraries, and animal shelters tell us what they need. We could have service during lunch or on school grounds so busy students can join without having to travel far. We could also give volunteers certificates or say their names at assemblies. When students see their classmates having fun with service and getting honored for it, more of them will want to join too.

I believe this plan will get more students into service on their own, and with better attitudes, than a rule ever could. Thank you for reading my opinion.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
